title: Session 1 — Participant 30 User + Claude Behavior Graphs
goal: Developing an architectural plan for Residential House
context: I have chosen this project because it requires a set of expertise to layout an architectural plan. Conditions including design brief, site and weather analysis, building codes, area and zoning standards to evaluate and design according to that as an expert.

Step 1.step_name: Summary of design brief, a set of requirements to start the project
Step 1.step_action: Prepare the design brief and define scope of project.

nodes.label: Checking out design briefs in the email, set up workspace, and submit design-brief prompt to Claude
nodes.detail: Downloads Residence CN.rvt from the linked Google Drive file, creates a local project folder with a personal notes file to assist during design, and launches the file in Revit 2027 while it loads in the background.

nodes.label: Generate comprehensive design brief document
nodes.detail: Loads its docx-authoring skill and produces a structured design brief covering priorities and program, room-by-room requirements, an area summary table, code/structural/MEP coordination notes, Revit deliverable scope, and an open-items list, then shares Design_Brief_Upper_Storey.docx.

nodes.label: Trying to remind herself what to do about the design plan in Revit and the design briefs, and reflecting on what to update/add to the design plan
Review and save the generated design brief document
nodes.detail: Opens the docx preview and reads through the Design Priorities, Site & Shell Parameters, and Area Summary sections to check the brief accurately reflects the client's requirements before requesting a location-specific version.

Step 2.step_name: area codes to use in project
Step 2.step_action: Ask about building codes and restrictions

nodes.label: Draft request for jurisdiction-specific design brief with code guidance referencing Reference.md
nodes.detail: While still reviewing the generic brief, types a follow-up prompt asking Claude to remake the design brief for a house in Oregon, USA, and to fold in local zoning height limits, fire-resistant wall requirements near property lines, roof-pitch/climate matching, second-floor load-bearing wall alignment, and stair placement strategy.

nodes.label: Generate a new design brief docx and ask flag jurisdiction ambiguity
Review the generated design brief document (v1)
nodes.detail: Opens the docx preview and reads through the Design Priorities, Site & Shell Parameters, and Area Summary sections to check the brief accurately reflects the client's requirements before requesting a location-specific version.

nodes.label: Specify Portland, Oregon as the project location
nodes.detail: Answers Claude's clarifying question, confirming the project site is in Portland, Oregon, so the correct zoning code section can be looked up.

nodes.label: Research Portland zoning/fire code and produce location-specific brief
nodes.detail: Runs web searches on Portland's Title 33 R5/R7/R10 zoning height and setback rules and the Oregon Residential Specialty Code's fire-resistance-near-property-line table, then generates and shares Design_Brief_Upper_Storey_Portland_OR.docx with the site/regulatory section added, flagging R5 as a working assumption pending confirmed zone.

nodes.label: Review and screenshot the newly generated design brief document with Portland specifications (v2)
Request a focused code reference reflected in the design brief after reviewing the Reference.md
Deliver consolidated residential code reference table
nodes.detail: Returns a table of Oregon Residential Specialty Code minimums for bedroom area, egress window dimensions, general window light/ventilation, ceiling height, and hallway clearance, with notes on sloped ceilings and above- vs below-grade egress differences.

nodes.label: Review the generated residential code reference table and clarify that only the second floor is being designed
Tighten code reference to second-floor specifics
nodes.detail: Re-issues the code table scoped to above-grade requirements only (using the 5.7 sq ft egress figure, not the grade-level exception) and flags a window fall-protection requirement relevant to second-floor bedroom and play-area windows, recommending it be locked into the Revit window family early.

nodes.label: Review Claude's response about Tighten code reference to second-floor specifics and Revit project

Step 3.step_name: plan zoning and divisions of spaces

nodes.label: Upload existing shell plan and request a full room layout
nodes.detail: Uploads an image of the existing 2nd-floor shell (upper deck, stairs, mechanical closet already drawn) and asks Claude to generate a layout of spaces based on the design brief and all the code standards discussed so far.

nodes.label: Generate first-pass SVG floor-plan layout (v1)
nodes.detail: Analyzes the shell geometry and maps the program onto it: Bedroom 1 in the north bump-out, Bedroom 2 and the Common Bath stacked in the west bay opening onto the hall, an L-shaped hall connecting the stair landing to both bedrooms, and the play area given the remaining volume with south-facing glazing; renders and cleans up the SVG before sharing Second_Floor_Proposed_Layout.svg with a rationale and flagged open items (property-line proximity, tub load path, assumed north).

nodes.label: Download the Design_Brief_Upper_Storey_Portland_OR.docx
nodes.detail: Downloads the Design_Brief_Upper_Storey_Portland_OR.docx generated by Claude.

nodes.label: Check the Floor Plan layout in Revit
nodes.detail: Reviews the v1 layout, then uploads the first-floor plan and asks that its walls be continued onto the 2nd floor, that Bedroom 1 and the play area be swapped for better north-facing light, that storage be added, and that the common bath be centered between both bedrooms.

nodes.label: Evaluate generated floor plan layout v1 against the floor plan in Revit
Issue a combined revision brief with first-floor reference
nodes.detail: Uploads the first-floor plan and asks that its walls be continued onto the 2nd floor, that Bedroom 1 and the play area be swapped for better north-facing light, that storage be added, and that the common bath be centered between both bedrooms.

nodes.label: Regenerate layout applying the swap and centering instructions (v2)
nodes.detail: Swaps the play area into the north bump-out (citing its even, glare-free light), grows Bedroom 1 into the vacated south block as an L-shaped room, centers the Common Bath between both bedrooms (now interior and mechanically vented), adds two storage closets, fixes a stray wall-line rendering bug, and shares Second_Floor_Layout_Revised.svg with a written rationale and trade-off notes.

nodes.label: Review the proposed layout and compare it with the Revit floor plan
Attempt to open Canal v1.rvt in Revit and click to update Revit from 2026 to 2027
Screenshot the prompt and paste it into the email draft
Check newly generated Second floor proposed layout (v2)

Step 4.step_name: Arrangement of spaces and Finalizing layout
Step 4.step_action: area and dimensions layouting of spaces with basic component furniture.

nodes.label: Specify exact dimensions and circulation fixes, referencing the dimensions in Revit
nodes.detail: Provides precise dimensions for Bedroom 2 (11'-5"x11'-3") and Bedroom 1 (11'-9"x11'-3"), asks that the bathroom sit between both bedrooms but be accessed from outside the lobby via a vestibule, that storage move outside the bathroom, that the closet be shrunk and placed near Bedroom 2, and that the staircase stay exactly as-is.

nodes.label: Deliver dimensioned layout (v3)
nodes.detail: Applies the exact bedroom dimensions, inserts a Vestibule for bath access off the Lobby (mirroring the first floor's own Vestibule-to-Bath precedent), relocates storage next to the vestibule entrance, shrinks and repositions the closet beside Bedroom 2, leaves the staircase untouched, and shares Second_Floor_Layout_V3.svg while flagging that Bedroom 1 now has only one exterior wall for egress.

nodes.label: Evaluate pros and cons of v3's circulation
nodes.detail: Talks through the v3 layout on camera, judging the lobby-as-passage-to-the-play-area and the storage/staircase placement as impractical while affirming the bedroom and bathroom zoning is good, concludes the AI-assisted layout phase is complete

Step 5.step_action: drafting architectural plan with basic component furniture.

nodes.label: Reconstruct walls and room partitions in Revit from the finalized concept
nodes.detail: Working alone in Revit 2027 with no further Claude interaction, extends and aligns the exterior walls into a consistent grid, then builds interior partitions for both bedrooms, the common bath, closets, storage, and the lobby — keeping Claude's liked bedroom/bathroom zoning but correcting the lobby and storage circulation issues just identified.

nodes.label: Place doors
nodes.detail: Adds door swings throughout the plan.

nodes.label: Place windows, and bathroom fixtures
nodes.detail: Places the bathtub, toilet, and single vanity/sink in the common bathroom to match the client brief's single-vanity-plus-bathtub priority.

nodes.label: Add room labels, dimensions, and complete the finalized floor plan
nodes.detail: Tags each space (Play Area, Upper Deck, Closet 1/2, Storage, Bedroom 1/2, Bath, Mech, Stairs) with text notes and adds dimension strings for each room, completing the finalized second-floor drafted plan with walls, doors, fixtures, and labels in place.
